units.zh: 慕容垂
units.en: Murong Chui
units.literal: Murong Chui

units.zh: 慕容垂，字道明，皝之第五子也。
units.en: Murong Chui, whose courtesy name was Daoming, was the fifth son of Murong Huang.
units.literal: Murong Chui, courtesy name Daoming, was the fifth son of Huang.

units.zh: 少岐嶷有器度，身長七尺七寸，手垂過膝。
units.en: As a youth he was unusually sharp and possessed great presence; he stood seven chi seven cun tall, and his hands reached below his knees.
units.literal: In youth he was precocious and had breadth of character; his height was seven chi seven cun, and his hands hung past his knees.

units.zh: 皝甚寵之，常目而謂諸弟曰：「此兒闊達好奇，終能破人家，或能成人家。」
units.en: Huang doted on him and would often look him in the eye and tell his younger brothers, "This boy is open-handed and restless; in the end he will either ruin a house or perhaps build one."
units.literal: Huang greatly favored him and would often fix his gaze on him and tell his younger brothers, "This boy is broad-minded and fond of novelty; in the end he will be able to destroy a household, or perhaps to establish one."

units.zh: 故名霸，字道業，恩遇逾於世子俊，故俊不能平之。
units.en: For this reason he was named Ba, with the courtesy name Daoye; the favor shown him surpassed that given the heir apparent Murong Jun, and Jun never made his peace with it.
units.literal: Therefore he was named Ba, courtesy name Daoye; favor shown him exceeded that of the heir apparent Jun, so Jun could not be reconciled to it.

units.zh: 以滅宇文之功，封都鄉侯。
units.en: For his part in the destruction of the Yuwen, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duxiang.
units.literal: For the achievement of destroying the Yuwen, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duxiang.

units.zh: 石季龍來伐，既還，猶有兼併之志，遣將鄧恆率眾數萬屯于樂安，營攻取之備。
units.en: After Shi Hu had invaded and withdrawn, he still intended to annex Yan and sent the general Deng Heng with tens of thousands of men to camp at Le'an, making ready to attack and take new territory.
units.literal: When Shi Jilong came to attack and had returned, he still harbored designs of annexation and sent the general Deng Heng to lead tens of thousands to encamp at Le'an, preparing camps for attack and seizure.

units.zh: 垂戍徒河，與恆相持，恆憚而不敢侵。
units.en: Chui held Tuhe and locked horns with Heng; Heng was afraid of him and did not dare advance.
units.literal: Chui garrisoned Tuhe and faced Heng in stalemate; Heng feared him and did not dare invade.

units.zh: 垂少好畋遊，因獵墜馬折齒，慕容俊僭即王位，改名𡙇，外以慕郤𡙇為名，內實惡而改之。
units.en: Chui had loved the chase since boyhood; on a hunt he fell from his horse and broke his teeth. When Murong Jun arrogated the royal title he changed Chui's name to 𡙇, claiming outwardly to admire Xi 𡙇 while in truth he loathed the character and altered it.
units.literal: Chui in youth loved hunting; while hunting he fell from his horse and broke his teeth. Murong Jun presumptuously assumed the royal title and changed his name to 𡙇, outwardly taking the name in admiration of Xi 𡙇, inwardly in fact detesting it and changing it.

units.zh: 尋以讖記之文，乃去「夬」，以「垂」為名焉。
units.en: Before long, following a prophetic text, he dropped the component "guai" and had his name fixed as "Chui".
units.literal: Soon, on the text of a prophecy, he removed the component "guai" and took "chui" as the name.

units.zh: 石季龍之死也，趙魏亂，垂謂俊曰：「時來易失，赴機在速，兼弱攻昧，今其時矣。」
units.en: When Shi Hu died and Zhao and Wei were in turmoil, Chui told Jun, "Moments like this are easily lost and must be seized at once—strike the weak while they are blind to danger; the hour is now."
units.literal: At the death of Shi Jilong, Zhao and Wei fell into disorder; Chui said to Jun, "Opportunity easily slips away; seizing the moment lies in speed—attacking the weak while they are still in the dark: now is the time."

units.zh: 俊以新遭大喪，不許。
units.en: Jun, still in mourning for his father, refused.
units.literal: Jun, having newly suffered a great bereavement, did not permit it.

units.zh: 慕輿根言於俊曰：「王子之言，千載一時，不可失也。」
units.en: Muyu Gen urged Jun, "What the prince says comes once in an age and must not be missed."
units.literal: Muyu Gen said to Jun, "The prince's words are a once-in-a-thousand-years moment and must not be lost."

units.zh: 俊乃從之，以垂為前鋒都督。
units.en: Jun took his counsel and made Chui commander of the vanguard.
units.literal: Jun then followed this advice and appointed Chui commander of the vanguard.

units.zh: 俊既克幽州，將坑降卒，垂諫曰：「吊伐之義，先代常典。
units.en: Once Jun had captured Youzhou and was set to slaughter the surrendered troops, Chui remonstrated, "To comfort the afflicted and chastise the wicked is the constant practice of former ages.
units.literal: After Jun had taken Youzhou and was about to bury alive the surrendered soldiers, Chui remonstrated, "The principle of succoring the fallen and punishing the guilty is an ancient constant.

units.zh: 今方平中原，宜綏懷以德，坑戮之刑不可為王師之先聲。」
units.en: As we are on the verge of pacifying the Central Plains, we should win hearts with virtue; mass execution must not be the first note struck by the king's army."
units.literal: Now as we are about to pacify the Central Plains, we ought to win men by kindness and virtue; the punishment of burial and slaughter must not be the royal army's first sound."

units.zh: 俊從之。
units.en: Jun accepted his advice.
units.literal: Jun followed this.

units.zh: 及俊僭稱尊號，封垂吳王，徙鎮信都，以侍中、右禁將軍錄留台事，大收東北之利。
units.en: When Jun took the imperial style, he enfeoffed Chui as Prince of Wu and posted him to Xindu as Palace Attendant and Right Forbidden General in charge of the capital secretariat, drawing great profit from the northeast.
units.literal: When Jun presumptuously assumed the exalted title, he enfeoffed Chui as Prince of Wu, transferred him to garrison Xindu, made him Palace Attendant and Right Forbidden General recording the affairs of the capital office, and greatly harvested the profits of the northeast.

units.zh: 又為征南將軍、荊、兗二州牧，有聲于梁、楚之南。
units.en: He was further appointed General Who Conquers the South and regional governor of Jing and Yan, winning fame throughout the lands south of the Huai.
units.literal: He was also made General Who Conquers the South and Governor of Jing and Yan provinces, gaining renown south of Liang and Chu.

units.zh: 再為司隸，偽王公已下莫不累跡。
units.en: Made Director of the Capital a second time, every man of rank in the Yan court thronged his gates.
units.literal: Again made Director of the Capital, none among the false princes and dukes downward failed to crowd his gate.

units.zh: 時莫容暐嗣偽位，慕容恪為太宰。
units.en: At that time Murong Wei held the throne and Murong Ke served as Grand Steward.
units.literal: At that time Murong Wei succeeded to the false throne and Murong Ke was Grand Steward.

units.zh: 恪甚重垂，常謂暐曰：「吳王將相之才十倍於臣，先帝以長幼之次，以臣先之，臣死之後，願陛下委政吳王，可謂親賢兼舉。」
units.en: Ke held Chui in the highest regard and often told Wei, "The Prince of Wu has ten times my gifts as statesman and commander; the late emperor set me above him only by birth order—when I am gone, entrust the realm to the Prince of Wu; that would be true love of worth and kin alike."
units.literal: Ke greatly valued Chui and often told Wei, "The Prince of Wu's talent as general and minister is ten times mine; the late emperor, because of order of seniority, placed me ahead of him—after I die, I hope Your Majesty will entrust government to the Prince of Wu; this may be called cherishing the worthy while elevating kin."

units.zh: 及敗桓溫於枋頭，威名大振。
units.en: After the victory over Huan Wen at Fangtou, his fame shook the realm.
units.literal: After defeating Huan Wen at Fangtou, his renown greatly shook the land.

units.zh: 慕容評深忌惡之，乃謀誅垂。
units.en: Murong Ping hated him bitterly and plotted his death.
units.literal: Murong Ping deeply hated him and plotted to kill Chui.

units.zh: 垂懼禍及己，與世子全奔於苻堅。
units.en: Fearing the blow would fall on him, Chui fled with the heir Quan to Fu Jian.
units.literal: Chui, fearing disaster would reach him, fled with the heir apparent Quan to Fu Jian.

units.zh: 自恪卒後，堅密有圖暐之謀，憚垂威名而未發。
units.en: After Ke's death Fu Jian secretly planned to destroy Yan but held back for fear of Chui's name.
units.literal: From the time Ke died, Jian secretly harbored designs on Wei but feared Chui's renown and did not act.

units.zh: 及聞其至，堅大悅，郊迎執手，禮之甚重。
units.en: Learning of his arrival, Fu Jian went out to meet him in the suburbs, took his hand, and honored him lavishly.
units.literal: When he heard Chui had arrived, Jian was greatly pleased, went out to the suburbs to meet him, took his hand, and treated him with the utmost honor.

units.zh: 堅相王猛惡垂雄略，勸堅殺之。
units.en: Fu Jian's chief minister Wang Meng detested Chui's daring and urged the emperor to kill him.
units.literal: Jian's chief minister Wang Meng hated Chui's bold strategy and urged Jian to kill him.

units.zh: 堅不從，以為冠軍將軍，封賓都侯，食華陰之五百戶。
units.en: Fu Jian refused; he appointed Chui General of the Champions and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Bintu with five hundred households at Huayin.
units.literal: Jian did not follow this; he made Chui General of the Champions and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Bintu with a fief of five hundred households at Huayin.

units.zh: 王猛伐洛，引全為參軍。
units.en: When Wang Meng attacked Luoyang he took Quan on as staff officer.
units.literal: Wang Meng attacked Luoyang and took Quan as aide.

units.zh: 猛乃令人詭傳垂語于全曰：「吾已東還，汝可為計也。」
units.en: Meng then had a man forge a message from Chui to Quan: "I have already gone east; make your own plans."
units.literal: Meng then had a man falsely spread word from Chui to Quan, "I have already returned east; you may make your plans."

units.zh: 全信之，乃奔暐。
units.en: Quan believed it and fled back to Murong Wei.
units.literal: Quan believed it and fled to Wei.

units.zh: 猛表全叛狀，垂懼而東奔，及藍田，為追騎所獲。
units.en: Meng reported Quan's treason; Chui fled east in alarm and was overtaken by pursuers at Lantian.
units.literal: Meng reported Quan's defection; Chui, in fear, fled east, and at Lantian was seized by pursuing horsemen.

units.zh: 堅引見東堂，慰勉之曰：「卿家國失和，委身投朕。
units.en: Fu Jian received him in the Eastern Hall and said kindly, "Your clan and your throne fell out, and you cast your lot with me.
units.literal: Jian summoned him to the Eastern Hall and comforted him, saying, "Your house and state were at odds and you entrusted yourself to Us.

units.zh: 賢子志不忘本，猶懷首丘。
units.en: Your worthy son has not forgotten his origins and still longs for his native hill.
units.literal: Your worthy son's will does not forget his roots and still cherishes his old mound.

units.zh: 《書》不云乎：「父父子子，無相及也。」
units.en: Does not the Documents say, "Father to father, son to son—neither shall harm the other"?"
units.literal: Does not the Book of Documents say, "Father is father, son is son—let none touch the other"?"

units.zh: 卿何為過懼而狼狽若斯也！」
units.en: Why then such panic and disorder!"
units.literal: Why then are you so excessively afraid and in such disarray!"

units.zh: 於是復垂爵位，恩待如初。
units.en: He then restored Chui's titles and treated him as before.
units.literal: Thereupon he restored Chui's rank and treated him with favor as before.

units.zh: 及堅擒暐，垂隨堅入鄴，收集諸子，對之悲慟，見其故吏，有不悅之色。
units.en: When Fu Jian took Murong Wei, Chui entered Ye with him, gathered his sons, and wept over them; at the sight of old retainers his face darkened.
units.literal: When Jian captured Wei, Chui followed Jian into Ye, gathered his sons, and wept before them; when he saw his former officials he showed displeasure.

units.zh: 前郎中令高弼私於垂曰：「大王以命世之姿，遭無妄之運，迍邅棲伏，艱亦至矣。
units.en: The former Master of Palace Gentlemen Gao Bi took Chui aside: "Your Highness, born to master an age, have met calamity without cause; long wandering and humbled, your hardship has reached its height.
units.literal: The former Master of Palace Gentlemen Gao Bi spoke privately to Chui, "Great King, with a world-ordering stature, you have met with unlooked-for fortune; wandering in hardship and dwelling in concealment, your trials have indeed reached their limit.

units.zh: 天啟嘉會，靈命暫遷，此乃鴻漸之始，龍變之初，深願仁慈有以慰之。
units.en: Heaven now opens a noble conjunction and the mandate briefly changes hands—this is the wild goose beginning its ascent, the dragon its first change; I pray Your Highness will take comfort in it.
units.literal: Heaven has opened a fine meeting; the mandate for the moment has shifted—this is the beginning of the wild goose's gradual ascent and the dragon's first transformation; I deeply hope Your benevolence may find comfort in this.

units.zh: 且夫高世之略必懷遺俗之規，方當網漏吞舟，以弘苞養之義；
units.en: A man who would tower above his age must keep counsels that ordinary men reject; now is the time to let the net spare the great fish and practice broad forbearance;
units.literal: Moreover, a strategy that towers above the age must harbor rules that depart from custom; one should now let the net leak great fish to enlarge the meaning of shelter and nurture;

units.zh: 收納舊臣之胄，以成為山之功，奈何以一怒捐之？
units.en: call home the sons of your old servants and build a mountain of loyalty—how can you throw them away in a fit of rage?
units.literal: gather in the sons of old ministers to complete the achievement of a mountain, yet how can you cast them away in a moment of anger?

units.zh: 竊為大王不取。」
units.en: I do not think this worthy of Your Highness."
units.literal: Privately I deem this unworthy of Great King."

units.zh: 垂深納之。
units.en: Chui took the advice to heart.
units.literal: Chui deeply accepted this.

units.zh: 垂在堅朝，歷位京兆尹，進封泉州侯，所在征伐，皆在大功。
units.en: In Fu Jian's service he became Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, was promoted to Marquis of Quanzhou, and wherever he campaigned he won the chief honors.
units.literal: While Chui was in Jian's court he rose to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, was advanced to Marquis of Quanzhou, and in every campaign he was assigned bore the greatest merit.

units.zh: 堅之敗於淮南也，垂軍獨全，堅以千餘騎奔垂。
units.en: When Fu Jian was broken at Huainan, only Chui's corps came through whole; Fu Jian rode to him with a little over a thousand men.
units.literal: When Jian was defeated at Huainan, Chui's army alone remained intact; Jian fled to Chui with a little more than a thousand horsemen.

units.zh: 垂世子寶言於垂曰：「家國傾喪，皇綱廢馳，至尊明命著之圖籙，當隆中興之業，建少康之功。
units.en: Chui's heir Murong Bao urged him, "Our house is fallen and the imperial order shattered; heaven's mandate is written in the charts—you should restore the dynasty as Shaokang did.
units.literal: Chui's heir Bao said to Chui, "House and state have toppled, the imperial norm lies in ruins; the Supreme One's bright mandate is marked in the charts and you should raise the work of restoration and build the achievement of Shaokang.

units.zh: 但時來之運未至，故韜光俟奮耳。
units.en: Only the hour had not come, and so you banked your fire and waited.
units.literal: Only the time's fortune had not yet come, so you hid your light and waited to spring.

units.zh: 今天厭亂德，凶眾土崩，可謂乾啟神機，授之於我。
units.en: Now heaven loathes their disorder, their hosts are collapsing—Qian has opened the divine moment and given it into our hands.
units.literal: Today heaven detests chaotic virtue, the wicked masses crumble—this may be called Qian opening the divine opportunity and handing it to us.

units.zh: 千載一時，今其會也，宜恭承皇天之意，因而取之。
units.en: A moment that comes once in an age is upon us; bow to heaven's will and seize it.
units.literal: A once-in-a-thousand-years moment—now is its conjunction; you should respectfully receive heaven's intent and take advantage of it.

units.zh: 且夫立大功者不顧小節，行大仁者不念小惠。
units.en: He who builds a great deed does not stumble over small scruples; he who practices great kindness does not count petty debts.
units.literal: Moreover, he who would achieve a great deed does not fuss over small points; he who would practice great benevolence does not dwell on small favors.

units.zh: 秦既蕩覆二京，空辱神器，仇恥之深，莫甚於此，願不以意氣微恩而忘社稷之重。
units.en: Qin has already overrun the Two Capitals and shamed the sacred vessel; no grudge runs deeper—do not let a private debt outweigh the altars of state.
units.literal: Qin has already swept away the Two Capitals and left the sacred vessel empty in shame; no hatred runs deeper—may you not, for a personal kindness, forget the weight of the altars.

units.zh: 五木之祥，今其至矣。」
units.en: The omen of the five woods has come to pass."
units.literal: The omen of the five woods has now arrived."

units.zh: 垂曰：「汝言是也。
units.en: Chui said, "You speak truly.
units.literal: Chui said, "Your words are right.

units.zh: 然彼以赤心投命，若何害之！
units.en: Yet he came to us with an open heart—how could we strike him down!
units.literal: Yet he entrusted himself to us with a loyal heart—how could we harm him!

units.zh: 苟天所棄，圖之多便。
units.en: If heaven has cast him off, there will be no lack of chances to destroy him.
units.literal: If heaven has abandoned him, plotting against him will be easy enough.

units.zh: 且縱令北還，更待其釁，既不負宿心，可以義取天下。」
units.en: Even if we let him ride north and wait for his next fault, we keep our old honor and may still win the realm in the name of justice."
units.literal: And even if we let him return north and wait again for his offense, we shall not betray our old resolve and may yet take the realm by right."

units.zh: 垂弟德進曰：「夫鄰國相吞，有自來矣。
units.en: His brother Murong De pressed him: "Neighboring states devour one another—that is the way of the world.
units.literal: Chui's younger brother De advanced and said, "Neighboring states swallow one another—this has always been so.

units.zh: 秦強而並燕，秦弱而圖之，此為報仇雪辱，豈所謂負宿心也！
units.en: Qin swallowed Yan when it was strong; we plot against Qin now that it is weak—this is vengeance, not betrayal of an old debt!
units.literal: When Qin was strong it annexed Yan; when Qin is weak we plot against it—this is to avenge and wipe away shame; how is it "betraying an old resolve"!"

units.zh: 昔鄧祁侯不納三甥之言，終為楚所滅；
units.en: The Marquis of Deng ignored his three nephews' counsel and was destroyed by Chu;
units.literal: In former times the Marquis of Deng did not heed the words of his three nephews and in the end was destroyed by Chu;

units.zh: 吳王夫差違子胥之諫，取禍句踐。
units.en: King Fuchai of Wu rejected Wu Zixu and brought ruin on himself at the hands of Goujian.
units.literal: King Fuchai of Wu went against Wu Zixu's remonstrance and brought disaster from Goujian.

units.zh: 前事之不忘，後事之師表也。
units.en: What went before, if not forgotten, teaches what comes after.
units.literal: Not to forget what went before is to take earlier events as teacher and model.

units.zh: 願不棄湯、武之成蹤，追韓信之敗跡，乘彼土崩，恭行天罰，斬逆氐，復宗祀，建中興，繼洪烈，天下大機，弗宜失也。
units.en: Do not turn from the path of Tang and Wu; remember how Han Xin fell; ride their collapse, execute heaven's punishment in earnest, slay the Di usurpers, restore the ancestral rites, raise a new age and continue the great work—the realm's great chance must not slip away.
units.literal: I pray you will not abandon the completed tracks of Tang and Wu, will pursue the trail of Han Xin's defeat, ride their crumbling earth, reverently execute heaven's punishment, cut down the rebellious Di, restore the ancestral sacrifices, establish restoration, continue the great enterprise—the great chance of the realm must not be lost.

units.zh: 若釋數萬之眾，授幹將之柄，是郤天時而待後害，非至計也。
units.en: To release tens of thousands of men and put the sword in his hand is to refuse heaven's season and invite later disaster—not supreme strategy.
units.literal: If you release tens of thousands of troops and hand the sword's hilt to the enemy, you reject heaven's season and wait for later harm—this is no supreme plan.

units.zh: 語曰：'當斷不斷，反受其亂。
units.en: The proverb says, "He who will not decide when he must, suffers chaos in the end."
units.literal: The saying runs, "When one should cut and does not, one suffers disorder in turn."

units.zh: '願兄無疑。」
units.en: Brother, put doubt aside.”
units.literal: Brother, harbor no doubt.”

units.zh: 垂曰：「吾昔為太傅所不容，投身于秦主，又為王猛所譖，復見昭亮，國士之禮每深，報德之分未一。
units.en: Chui answered, "Once the Grand Tutor would not keep me and I threw myself on the Qin ruler; Wang Meng slandered me, yet Fu Jian cleared me; he treated me as a champion of the realm, and I have scarcely begun to repay him.
units.literal: Chui said, "In former days I was not tolerated by the Grand Tutor and threw myself on the Lord of Qin; again Wang Meng slandered me, yet I was again shown clear favor; the rites due a champion of the state were ever deep, yet I have not repaid a fraction of the debt.

units.zh: 如使秦運必窮，歷數歸我者，授首之便，何慮無之。
units.en: If Qin's mandate is truly spent and the succession returns to us, the chance to take his head will come—why fear it will not?
units.literal: If Qin's fortune must indeed reach its end and the succession should return to us, the convenience of taking his head—why worry that it will not come?

units.zh: 關西之地，會非吾有，自當有擾之者，吾可端拱而定關東。
units.en: The west of the Pass was never ours; others will tear it apart—I may fold my hands and secure the east.
units.literal: The lands west of the Pass were never mine to hold; there will be others to trouble them—I can sit with folded hands and settle the east of the Pass.

units.zh: 君子不怙亂，不為禍先，且可觀之。」
units.en: A gentleman does not profit from chaos or invite disaster before its time; for now let us wait and see."
units.literal: A gentleman does not rely on disorder and does not beget calamity first; for the present let us watch."

units.zh: 乃以兵屬堅。
units.en: He then placed his troops at Fu Jian's disposal.
units.literal: Thereupon he turned his troops over to Jian.

units.zh: 初，寶在長安，與韓黃、李根等因讌摴蒱，寶危坐整容，誓之曰：「世云摴蒱有神，豈虛也哉！
units.en: Earlier, while Bao was at Chang'an, he played chupu at a feast with Han Huang, Li Gen, and others; sitting rigidly upright he swore, "Men say the gaming pieces have a god—surely that is no idle tale!
units.literal: Earlier, when Bao was at Chang'an, he attended a banquet with Han Huang, Li Gen, and others and played chupu; Bao sat upright, composed his expression, and swore, "The world says chupu has a god—is this empty talk!

units.zh: 若富貴可期，頻得三盧。」
units.en: If fortune is ordained for me, let me throw three "lu" in a row."
units.literal: If wealth and honor may be foreseen, let me throw three "lu" in succession."

units.zh: 於是三擲盡盧，寶拜而受賜，故云五木之祥。
units.en: He cast three times and each throw was lu; Bao bowed to accept the sign—hence "the omen of the five woods."
units.literal: Thereupon he cast three times and all were lu; Bao bowed and accepted the omen—hence the words "omen of the five woods."

units.zh: 堅至澠池，垂請至鄴展拜陵墓，因張國威刑，以安戎狄。
units.en: When Fu Jian came to Mianchi, Chui asked leave to go to Ye to worship at the tombs and, by a show of imperial law, to quiet the frontier peoples.
units.literal: When Jian reached Mianchi, Chui requested to go to Ye to perform obeisance at the tombs and, by displaying the state's majesty and punishments, to pacify the barbarians.

units.zh: 堅許之，權翼諫曰：「垂爪牙名將，所謂今之韓、白，世豪東夏，志不為人用。
units.en: Fu Jian agreed; Quan Yi objected, "Chui is a fang-and-claw commander, a Han Xin or Bai Qi of our day, a champion of the eastern lands who will not serve another's will.
units.literal: Jian permitted it; Quan Yi remonstrated, "Chui is a fang-and-claw famous general, what men call today's Han Xin and Bai Qi; a hero of the eastern Xia whose will is not to serve another.

units.zh: 頃以避禍歸誠，非慕德而至，列土幹城未可以滿其志，冠軍之號豈足以稱其心！
units.en: He came lately only to escape ruin, not from love of your virtue; lands and commands cannot satisfy him, and the rank of champion is too small for his pride!
units.literal: Recently he returned in sincerity to escape disaster, not from admiration of virtue; fiefs and garrison posts cannot fill his ambition, and the title General of the Champions is hardly enough for his heart!

units.zh: 且垂猶鷹也，饑則附人，飽便高颺，遇風塵之會，必有陵霄之志。
units.en: Chui is like a hawk: hungry he perches on your wrist, fed he mounts to the sky; give him a season of turmoil and he will aim for the clouds.
units.literal: Moreover Chui is like a hawk: hungry he clings to men, sated he soars high; meeting a season of wind and dust he is sure to harbor the will to pierce the clouds.

units.zh: 惟宜急其羈靽，不可任其所欲。」
units.en: Tighten his bridle at once; do not let him have his way."
units.literal: You should only hasten his bridle and reins and must not leave him to his desires."

units.zh: 堅不從，遣其將李蠻、閔亮、尹國率眾三千送垂，又遣石越戍鄴，張蠔戍并州。
units.en: Fu Jian refused; he sent Li Man, Min Liang, and Yin Guo with three thousand men to escort Chui, posted Shi Yue at Ye and Zhang Ni at Bingzhou.
units.literal: Jian did not follow this; he sent his generals Li Man, Min Liang, and Yin Guo with three thousand men to escort Chui, and also sent Shi Yue to garrison Ye and Zhang Ni to garrison Bingzhou.

units.zh: 時堅子丕先在鄴，及垂至，丕館之於鄴西，垂具說淮南敗狀。
units.en: Fu Jian's son Fu Pi was already at Ye; when Chui arrived, Pi lodged him west of the city while Chui reported the disaster at Huainan in detail.
units.literal: At that time Jian's son Pi was already at Ye; when Chui arrived, Pi lodged him west of Ye, and Chui set forth in full the defeat at Huainan.

units.zh: 會堅將苻暉告丁零翟斌聚眾謀逼洛陽，歪謂垂曰：「惟斌兄弟因王師小失，敢肆凶勃，子母之軍，殆難為敵，非冠軍英略，莫可以滅也。
units.en: Just then Fu Jian's general Fu Hui reported that the Dingling leader Zhai Bin had raised a host against Luoyang; Fu Pi told Chui, "Bin and his brothers, exploiting our recent setback, dare rise in violence; a mother-and-son force is a hard match—only your brilliance can break them.
units.literal: It happened that Jian's general Fu Hui reported that the Dingling Zhai Bin had gathered a host to press Luoyang; Pi said to Chui, "Bin and his brothers, taking advantage of a small defeat of the royal army, dare commit outrage; mother and son together are nearly a match—none but the champion's brilliant plan can destroy them.

units.zh: 欲相煩一行可乎？」
units.en: Will you undertake this campaign for me?"
units.literal: May I trouble you to go on one expedition?"

units.zh: 垂曰：「下官殿下之鷹犬，敢不惟命是聽。」
units.en: Chui said, "I am the hound at Your Highness's heel—how should I not obey?"
units.literal: Chui said, "Your servant is the hound and falcon at my lord's side—how should I not obey every command?"

units.zh: 於是大賜金帛，一無所受，惟請舊田園。
units.en: He was offered gold and silk in abundance but took none, asking only for his former estates.
units.literal: Thereupon he was greatly rewarded with gold and silks but accepted none, asking only for his old fields and gardens.

units.zh: 丕許之，配垂兵二千，遣其將苻飛龍率氐騎一千為垂之副。
units.en: Pi agreed, gave him two thousand men, and sent Fu Feilong with a thousand Di cavalry as his second.
units.literal: Pi permitted this, assigned Chui two thousand troops, and sent his general Fu Feilong with a thousand Di horsemen as Chui's deputy.

units.zh: 丕戒飛龍曰：「卿王室肺腑，年秩雖卑，其實帥也。
units.en: Pi warned Feilong, "You are of the imperial blood; young as you are, you are in truth the commander.
units.literal: Pi admonished Feilong, "You are flesh of the royal house; though young in years, in truth you are the commander.

units.zh: 垂為三軍之統，卿為謀垂之主，用兵制勝之權，防微杜貳之略，委之於卿，卿其勉之。」
units.en: Chui leads the host, but you are to plot against him—the right to command, the watch against treason, all rest with you; do your utmost."
units.literal: Chui commands the three armies; you are master of the plan against Chui—the power to use troops and win, the strategy to guard against the first stirrings of rebellion, are entrusted to you; exert yourself."

units.zh: 垂請入鄴城拜廟，丕不許。
units.en: Chui asked to enter Ye and worship at the ancestral shrine; Pi refused.
units.literal: Chui requested to enter Ye city to worship at the temple; Pi did not permit it.

units.zh: 乃潛服而入，亭吏禁之，垂怒，斬吏燒亭而去。
units.en: He slipped in disguised; the gate officer stopped him, and Chui in fury killed the man, burned the post, and rode away.
units.literal: He then entered secretly in plain dress; the post-station clerk barred him, and in anger Chui killed the clerk, burned the station, and left.

units.zh: 石越言於丕曰：「垂之在燕，破國亂家，及投命聖朝，蒙超常之遇，忽敢輕侮方鎮，殺吏焚亭，反形已露，終為亂階。
units.en: Shi Yue urged Pi, "In Yan, Chui broke state and house; received here with extraordinary grace, he now insults your command, kills your officer and burns his post—rebellion is plain and he will be our ruin.
units.literal: Shi Yue said to Pi, "When Chui was in Yan he ruined the state and troubled the house; having entrusted himself to the holy dynasty he received favor beyond measure, yet he suddenly dared insult the regional commander, kill the clerk and burn the station—the shape of rebellion is already exposed and in the end he will be a source of disorder.

units.zh: 將老兵疲，可襲而取之矣。」
units.en: His generals are old and his soldiers weary—strike now and take him."
units.literal: His generals are old and his soldiers weary—he may be attacked and taken."

units.zh: 歪曰：「淮南之敗，眾散親離，而垂侍衛聖躬，誠不可忘。」
units.en: Pi said, "After Huainan the army broke and families scattered, yet Chui guarded the Son of Heaven—that debt must not be forgotten."
units.literal: Pi said, "At the defeat in Huainan the host scattered and kin were parted, yet Chui guarded the sacred person—this faithfulness truly must not be forgotten."

units.zh: 越曰：「垂既不忠於燕，其肯盡忠於我乎！
units.en: Yue replied, "He was not loyal to Yan—will he be loyal to us?
units.literal: Yue said, "Since Chui was not loyal to Yan, will he be wholly loyal to us!

units.zh: 且其亡虜也，主上寵同功舊，不能銘澤誓忠，而首謀為亂，今不擊之，必為後害。」
units.en: He is a defeated foe whom the emperor honored like an old companion; instead of gratitude he plots revolt—if you do not strike now, he will destroy us later."
units.literal: Moreover he is a captive whom the sovereign favored like an old merit-holder; unable to engrave grace and swear loyalty, he is first to plot disorder—if you do not strike now, he will surely harm us later."

units.zh: 丕不從。
units.en: Pi would not listen.
units.literal: Pi did not follow this.

units.zh: 越退而告人曰：「公父子好存小仁，不顧天下大計，吾屬終當為鮮卑虜矣。」
units.en: Yue withdrew and said, "Father and son cherish petty kindness and forget the realm's great design—we shall end as captives of the Xianbei."
units.literal: Yue withdrew and told others, "The lord and son love to keep small kindness and disregard the great plan of the realm—we shall in the end become captives of the Xianbei."

units.zh: 垂至河內，殺飛龍，悉誅氐兵，召募遠近，眾至三萬，濟河焚橋，令曰：「吾本外假秦聲，內規興復。
units.en: At Henei Chui killed Feilong, slaughtered the Di detachment, and raised men until his host numbered thirty thousand; he crossed the Yellow River, burned the bridge, and proclaimed, "Outwardly I borrowed Qin's name; inwardly I sought to restore my house.
units.literal: Chui reached Henei, killed Feilong, executed all the Di soldiers, recruited far and near, and his host reached thirty thousand; he crossed the river and burned the bridge, issuing an order, "I originally borrowed Qin's name outwardly while inwardly planning restoration.

units.zh: 亂法者軍有常刑，奉命者賞不逾日，天下既定，封爵有差，不相負也。」
units.en: Break discipline and the army's law will find you; obey and reward comes before the sun sets; when the realm is settled, rank and fief will be justly apportioned—no man cheated of his due."
units.literal: Those who disturb the law will suffer the army's constant punishments; those who obey orders will be rewarded within the day; when the realm is settled, ranks and fiefs will be graded—none will be cheated."

units.zh: 翟斌聞垂之將濟河也，遣使推垂為盟主。
units.en: Learning that Chui was about to cross the Yellow River, Zhai Bin sent envoys offering to make him leader of the alliance.
units.literal: When Zhai Bin heard Chui was about to cross the river, he sent envoys to urge Chui as league chief.

units.zh: 垂距之曰：「吾父子寄命秦朝，危而獲濟，荷主上不世之恩，蒙更生之惠，雖曰君臣，義深父子，豈可因其小隙，便懷二三。
units.en: Chui declined: "My son and I cast our lot with Qin in mortal danger and were spared; we owe the emperor a grace beyond measure and life itself—though called subject and lord, our bond is that of father and son; how could a small quarrel make us waver in loyalty?
units.literal: Chui refused, saying, "My son and I entrusted our lives to the Qin court; in peril we were saved, bearing the sovereign's unworldly grace and receiving the favor of renewed life—though called minister and ruler, our bond is as deep as father and son; how can we, for a small rift, harbor divided loyalties.

units.zh: 吾本救豫州，不赴君等，何為斯議而及於我！」
units.en: I came to save Yuzhou, not to join your cause—why drag me into this!"
units.literal: I came originally to rescue Yuzhou, not to join you—why does this proposal touch me!"

units.zh: 垂進欲襲據洛陽，故見苻暉以臣節，退又未審斌之誠款，故以此言距之。
units.en: He still meant to take Luoyang, so he treated Fu Hui as his sovereign; uncertain of Bin's good faith, he answered with this refusal.
units.literal: Chui advanced intending to seize Luoyang, so he showed Fu Hui the forms of a subject; afterward, not yet sure of Bin's sincerity, he used these words to refuse.

units.zh: 垂至洛陽，暉閉門距守，不與垂通。
units.en: At Luoyang, Fu Hui shut the gates and would not treat with him.
units.literal: Chui reached Luoyang; Hui closed the gates and held defense, not communicating with Chui.

units.zh: 斌又遣長史河南郭通說垂，乃許之。
units.en: Bin sent his chief clerk Guo Tong of Henan to persuade him, and Chui consented.
units.literal: Bin again sent the Chief Clerk of Henan Guo Tong to persuade Chui, and Chui then agreed.

units.zh: 斌率眾會垂，勸稱尊號，垂曰：「新興侯，國之正統，孤之君也。
units.en: Bin brought his forces to Chui and urged him to take the imperial title; Chui said, "The Marquis of Xinxing is the rightful heir and my sovereign.
units.literal: Bin led his host to join Chui and urged him to assume the exalted title; Chui said, "The Marquis of Xinxing is the state's legitimate line and my lord.

units.zh: 若以諸君之力，得平關東，當以大義喻秦，奉迎反正。
units.en: If your strength can settle the east, we should teach Qin its duty and restore the rightful ruler.
units.literal: If by your strength we can pacify the east of the Pass, we should instruct Qin with great principle and welcome the return to the right.

units.zh: 無上自尊，非孤心也。」
units.en: To set myself above my lord is not my wish."
units.literal: To exalt oneself without a superior is not my heart."

units.zh: 謀於眾曰：「洛陽四面受敵，北阻大河，至於控馭燕、趙，非形勝之便，不如北取鄴都，據之而制天下。」
units.en: He asked his officers: "Luoyang is beset on every side and barred by the Yellow River; it is no place to command Yan and Zhao—better to seize Ye in the north and rule the realm from there."
units.literal: He consulted the assembly, saying, "Luoyang is attacked on four sides and blocked to the north by the great river; as for controlling Yan and Zhao, it is not a terrain of strategic advantage—better to take Ye in the north, hold it, and control the realm."

units.zh: 眾咸以為然。
units.en: All agreed.
units.literal: All agreed this was so.

units.zh: 乃引師而東，遣建威將軍王騰起浮橋于石門。
units.en: He marched east and sent General Who Establishes Might Wang Teng to build a pontoon bridge at Shimen.
units.literal: Thereupon he led the army east and sent the General Who Establishes Might Wang Teng to raise a pontoon bridge at Shimen.

units.zh: 初，垂之發鄴中，子農及兄子楷、紹，北子宙，為苻丕所留。
units.en: When Chui left Ye, his son Murong Nong, his nephews Kai and Shao, and his son Zhou had been left behind in Fu Pi's hands.
units.literal: Earlier, when Chui set out from Ye, his son Nong and his brother's sons Kai and Shao, and his northern son Zhou, were detained by Fu Pi.

units.zh: 及誅飛龍，遣田生密告農等，使起兵趙、魏以相應。
units.en: After he killed Feilong he sent Tian Sheng secretly to Nong and the others to raise the north in revolt.
units.literal: When Feilong was executed, he sent Tian Sheng in secret to inform Nong and the others to raise troops in Zhao and Wei in response.

units.zh: 於是農、宙奔列人，楷、紹奔辟陽，眾咸應之。
units.en: Nong and Zhou fled to Lieren, Kai and Shao to Piyang, and the people rose everywhere.
units.literal: Thereupon Nong and Zhou fled to Lieren, Kai and Shao to Piyang, and the masses all responded.

units.zh: 農西招庫辱官偉於上黨，東引乞特歸於東阿，各率眾數萬赴之，眾至十餘萬。
units.en: Nong won Guan Wei in Shangdang to the west and Qitegui at Dong'e to the east; each brought tens of thousands until their host passed a hundred thousand.
units.literal: Nong in the west recruited Guan Wei of the Kulumu office at Shangdang, in the east drew Qitegui at Dong'e—each led tens of thousands to come, and the host reached more than a hundred thousand.

units.zh: 丕遣石越討農，為農所敗，斬越于陳。
units.en: Fu Pi sent Shi Yue against Nong; Nong routed him and killed him at Chen.
units.literal: Pi sent Shi Yue to attack Nong; Nong defeated him and beheaded Yue at Chen.

units.zh: 垂引兵至滎陽，乙太元八年自稱大將軍、大都督、燕王，承制行事，建元曰燕元。
units.en: Chui advanced to Xingyang; in the eighth year of the Taiyuan era he proclaimed himself Grand General, Grand Commander, and Prince of Yan, acting with imperial authority under the era name Yan Yuan.
units.literal: Chui led troops to Xingyang; in the eighth year of the Taiyuan era he styled himself Grand General, Grand Commander, and Prince of Yan, acting by imperial commission, and established the era name Yan Yuan.

units.zh: 令稱統府，府置四佐，王公已下稱臣，凡所封拜，一如王者，以翟斌為建義大將軍，封河南王；
units.en: He styled his headquarters the Commandery Office with four aides; nobles and officials addressed him as lord; enfeoffments followed royal precedent; Zhai Bin became Grand General Who Establishes Righteousness and Prince of Henan;
units.literal: He ordered that the unified headquarters be called the Commandery Office, with four assistants; princes and dukes downward called him lord; all enfeoffments and appointments were as for a king; Zhai Bin was made Grand General Who Establishes Righteousness and Prince of Henan;

units.zh: 翟檀為柱國大將軍、弘農王；
units.en: Zhai Tan was made Grand General of the State and Prince of Hongnong;
units.literal: Zhai Tan was made Grand General of the State Pillar and Prince of Hongnong;

units.zh: 弟德為車騎大將軍、范陽王；
units.en: his brother De became Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Prince of Fanyang;
units.literal: his younger brother De was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Prince of Fanyang;

units.zh: 兄子楷征西大將軍、太原王。
units.en: his nephew Kai became General Who Conquers the West and Prince of Taiyuan.
units.literal: his brother's son Kai was made General Who Conquers the West and Prince of Taiyuan.

units.zh: 眾至二十餘萬，濟自石門，長驅攻鄴。
units.en: His army swelled past two hundred thousand; crossing at Shimen he marched on Ye in force.
units.literal: The host reached more than two hundred thousand; crossing from Shimen they drove in long columns to attack Ye.

units.zh: 農、楷、紹、宙等率眾會垂。
units.en: Nong, Kai, Shao, Zhou, and the rest joined him with their hosts.
units.literal: Nong, Kai, Shao, Zhou, and others led their hosts to join Chui.

units.zh: 立子寶為燕王太子，封功臣為公侯伯子男者百餘人。
units.en: He made Bao heir to Yan and enfeoffed more than a hundred ministers as dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons.
units.literal: He installed his son Bao as Heir Apparent of Yan and enfeoffed meritorious ministers as dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons—more than a hundred men.

units.zh: 苻丕乃遣侍郎姜讓謂垂曰：「往歲大駕失據，君保衛鑾輿，勤王誠義，邁蹤前烈。
units.en: Fu Pi sent the attendant Jiang Rang to say, "When the emperor lost his throne you guarded him; your loyalty outshone the ancients.
units.literal: Fu Pi then sent the Gentleman Attendant Jiang Rang to tell Chui, "In former years the imperial carriage lost its footing and you guarded the regalia, your loyal service to the throne surpassing the achievements of old.

units.zh: 宜述修前規，終忠貞之節，奈何棄崇山之功，為此過舉！
units.en: Continue on that path and keep faith to the end—why throw away a mountain of merit for this rash rebellion?
units.literal: You ought to continue the former plan and end in the integrity of loyal constancy—why abandon the achievement of a lofty mountain for this excessive act!

units.zh: 過貴能改，先賢之嘉事也。
units.en: To err and amend is the praise of sages.
units.literal: To pass is noble if one can reform—this is the praised deed of the sages.

units.zh: 深宜詳思，悟猶未晚。」
units.en: Think again; it is not too late to turn back."
units.literal: Deeply you should ponder; it is not yet late to awaken."

units.zh: 垂謂讓曰：「孤受主上不世之恩，故欲安全長樂公，使盡眾赴京師，然後修復家國之業，與秦永為鄰好。
units.en: Chui told Rang, "I owe the emperor a boundless debt; I wished to send the Duke of Changle with all his men to the capital, then restore my house and live at peace with Qin.
units.literal: Chui said to Rang, "I received the sovereign's unworldly grace and therefore wished to keep the Duke of Changle safe, have him send all his host to the capital, and then restore the house and state, remaining forever Qin's neighbor in good faith.

units.zh: 何故暗於機運，不以鄴見歸也？
units.en: Why does he refuse to read the times and yield Ye?
units.literal: Why is he dark to the turn of fortune and will not surrender Ye to me?

units.zh: 大義滅親，況于意氣之顧！
units.en: When great duty calls, kinship itself may be set aside—what is a private debt?
units.literal: Great righteousness destroys kin—how much more a bond of personal feeling!

units.zh: 公若迷而不返者，孤亦欲竊兵勢耳。
units.en: If you will not see reason, I must borrow the force of arms.
units.literal: If you are deluded and do not return, I too mean to borrow military force.

units.zh: 今事已然，恐單馬乞命不可得也。」
units.en: Matters have gone too far; do not expect mercy on a lone horse."
units.literal: Now the matter is already thus; I fear begging for my life on a single horse will not be obtainable."

units.zh: 讓厲色責垂曰：「將軍不容于家國，投命於聖朝，燕之尺土，將軍豈有分乎！
units.en: Rang rebuked him: "You were driven from your own land and the emperor took you in—what inch of Yan soil is yours?
units.literal: Rang sternly reproached Chui, "The general was not tolerated in his house and state and entrusted his life to the holy dynasty—the inch of Yan soil, does the general have a share in it!

units.zh: 主上與將軍風殊類別，臭味不同，奇將軍于一見，托將軍以斷金，寵逾宗舊，任齊懿籓，自古君臣冥契之重，豈甚此邪！
units.en: Emperor and subject are unlike in nature, yet he honored you at first sight, joined you in oath, favored you above his kin, and gave you power equal to a great prince—when was loyalty ever heavier?
units.literal: The sovereign and the general are of different winds and unlike kinds, different in taste—yet the sovereign at one meeting cherished the general, entrusted him with severed metal, favored him above clan elders, entrusted him equal to the most honored fiefs—since ancient times has the dark accord of ruler and minister been heavier than this!

units.zh: 方付將軍以六尺之孤，萬里之命，奈何王師小敗，便有二圖！
units.en: He would have entrusted his child and his realm to you—how, after one defeat, can you turn traitor?
units.literal: He was about to entrust the six-foot orphan and the mandate of ten thousand li to the general—how, at a small defeat of the royal army, can there be two designs!

units.zh: 夫師起無名，終則弗成，天之所廢，人不能支。
units.en: A war without just cause cannot succeed; what heaven casts off, no man can uphold.
units.literal: An army raised without a name in the end cannot succeed; what heaven abandons, man cannot support.

units.zh: 將軍起無名之師，而欲興天所廢，竊未見其可。
units.en: You make war without cause and hope to prosper what heaven has doomed—I do not see how that can stand.
units.literal: The general raises an army without a name and wishes to prosper what heaven abandons—I privately do not see how it can be done.

units.zh: 長樂公主上之元子，聲德邁于唐、衛，居陝東之任，為朝廷維城，其可束手輸將軍以百城之地！
units.en: The Duke of Changle is the emperor's eldest son, his virtue beyond Tang and Wei, the pillar east of the mountains—he will not meekly yield you a hundred cities!
units.literal: The Duke of Changle is the sovereign's eldest son, his virtue surpassing Tang and Wei, holding the duty east of Shan—he is the court's bulwark; how can he meekly hand the general a hundred cities!

units.zh: 大夫死王事，國君死社稷，將軍欲裂冠毀冕，拔本塞源者，自可任將軍兵勢，何復多雲。
units.en: Ministers die for their lord, rulers die for their altars—if you mean to tear the crown and uproot the dynasty, use your armies; words are wasted.
units.literal: Great officers die for the king's affair, the ruler dies for the altars—the general wishes to tear the cap and destroy the crown, uproot the source and block the spring: let the general use his military might as he will; why say more.

units.zh: 但念將軍以七十之年，懸首白旗，高世之忠，忽為逆鬼，竊為將軍痛之。」
units.en: Yet you are seventy; to hang your head on a white pole, to turn the loyalty of ages into the ghost of a rebel—that I grieve for you."
units.literal: Only consider that the general, at seventy years, will hang his head on a white flag—the loyalty of towering ages suddenly becomes a rebellious ghost; privately I grieve for the general."

units.zh: 垂默然。
units.en: Chui said nothing.
units.literal: Chui was silent.

units.zh: 左右勸垂殺之，垂曰：「古者兵交，使在其間，犬各吠非其主，何所問也！」
units.en: His attendants urged him to kill Rang; Chui said, "When armies meet, the envoy stands between them; dogs bark at strangers—why question him?"
units.literal: Those at his side urged Chui to kill him; Chui said, "In antiquity when armies met, the envoy remained between them; dogs each bark at what is not their master—what is there to ask!"

units.zh: 乃遣讓歸。
units.en: He sent Rang away unharmed.
units.literal: He then sent Rang back.

units.zh: 垂上表於苻堅曰：「臣才非古人，致禍起蕭牆，身嬰時難，歸命聖朝。
units.en: Chui wrote to Fu Jian: "I am no man of antiquity; trouble rose within the court, I fell on evil days, and cast myself on your mercy.
units.literal: Chui memorialized Fu Jian, saying, "Your servant's talent is not that of men of old; disaster arose within the palace walls, my person met the hardship of the times, and I entrusted my life to the holy dynasty.

units.zh: 陛下恩深周、漢，猥叨微顧之遇，位為列將，爵忝通侯，誓在戮力輸誠，常懼不及。
units.en: Your grace is deep as Zhou and Han; you raised me to rank and enfeoffed me as marquis, and I swore to serve with all my strength, ever fearing I fell short.
units.literal: Your Majesty's grace is deep as Zhou and Han; I humbly received the favor of a slight glance, was made a ranked general and enfeoffed as a full marquis, swearing to exert my strength in loyalty, ever fearing I could not suffice.

units.zh: 去夏桓沖送死，一擬雲消，回討鄖城，俘馘萬計，斯誠陛下神算之奇，頗亦愚臣忘死之效。
units.en: Last summer Huan Chong came courting death; at one stroke his forces scattered like clouds; we then attacked Yuncheng and took tens of thousands of captives and severed ears—this was your divine strategy and my small share in risking death for you.
units.literal: Last summer Huan Chong came courting death; at one stroke his forces dispersed like clouds; returning to attack Yuncheng, we took captives and severed ears by the tens of thousands—this was truly Your Majesty's divine calculation, and also the result of your foolish servant's disregard for death.

units.zh: 方將飲馬桂州，懸旌閩會，不圖天助亂德，大駕班師。
units.en: We meant to water our horses in Guizhou and plant our banners in Min and Hui, never dreaming heaven would favor disorder and the imperial march would turn back.
units.literal: I was about to water our horses at Guizhou and hang our banners at Min and Hui, not thinking heaven would aid chaotic virtue and the great carriage would withdraw its army.

units.zh: 陛下單馬奔臣，臣奉衛匪貳，豈陛下聖明鑒臣單心，皇天后土實亦知之。
units.en: You rode alone to me and I guarded you without fail—surely you see my heart, and heaven knows it too.
units.literal: Your Majesty on a single horse fled to your servant; your servant guarded and served without disloyalty—surely Your Majesty's sagely clarity sees your servant's single heart, and the August Lord Above and the August Lord Below in truth also know it.

units.zh: 臣奉詔北巡，受制長樂。
units.en: I was ordered north and bound by the Duke of Changle.
units.literal: Your servant received the edict to tour the north and was constrained by the Duke of Changle.

units.zh: 然丕外失眾心，內多猜忌，今臣野次外庭，不聽謁廟。
units.en: Pi lost the people and trusted no one; I camp outside the walls and may not enter the shrine.
units.literal: Yet Pi outwardly lost the hearts of the masses and inwardly harbored many suspicions; now your servant camps outside the court and is not permitted to worship at the temple.

units.zh: 丁零逆豎寇逼豫州，丕迫臣單赴，限以師程，惟給弊卒二千，盡無兵杖，復令飛龍潛為刺客。
units.en: The Dingling rebels press Yuzhou; Pi sent me with two thousand broken men and no arms, and set Feilong to murder me in secret.
units.literal: The Dingling rebel bandits press Yuzhou; Pi forced your servant to go alone, limiting the deadline, giving only two thousand worn troops without weapons, and again sent Feilong in secret as assassin.

units.zh: 及至洛陽，平原公暉復不信納。
units.en: At Luoyang Fu Hui, Duke of Pingyuan, would not trust me.
units.literal: When I reached Luoyang, Fu Hui, Duke of Pingyuan, again would not trust or accept me.

units.zh: 臣竊惟進無淮陰功高之慮，退無李廣失利之愆，懼有青蠅，交亂白黑，丁零夷夏以臣忠而見疑，乃推臣為盟主。
units.en: I had neither Han Xin's fear of too great merit nor Li Guang's blame for defeat; I feared slander; the Dingling, seeing me loyal yet distrusted, made me their chief.
units.literal: Your servant reflected that advancing I had not the worry of Huaiyin's towering merit, retreating I had not Li Guang's fault of defeat—I feared green flies would confound black and white; the Dingling, barbarian and Chinese alike, seeing your servant loyal yet suspected, then urged your servant as league chief.

units.zh: 臣受託善始，不遂令終，泣望西京，揮涕即邁。
units.en: I took their trust at the start and cannot end it cleanly; weeping I turn toward the western capital and march on.
units.literal: Your servant received the trust at the beginning and could not bring it to the end; weeping I gaze at the western capital and, brushing tears, set out.

units.zh: 軍次石門，所在雲赴，雖復周武之會于孟津，漢祖之集於垓下，不期之眾，實有甚焉。
units.en: At Shimen men flocked to us—greater than the hosts of King Wu at Mengjin or Han Gaozu at Gaixia.
units.literal: The army halted at Shimen; everywhere clouds gathered to join—though the assembly of Zhou Wu at Mengjin and Han Zu at Gaixia were unlooked-for hosts, in truth there were more than those.

units.zh: 欲令長樂公盡眾赴難，以禮發遣，而丕固守匹夫之志，不達變通之理。
units.en: I asked the Duke of Changle to send all his men to the emperor and release them with honor; Pi clung to his obstinacy and would not bend.
units.literal: I wished to have the Duke of Changle send all his host to the rescue and dismiss them with ceremony, but Pi obstinately held the will of a common man and did not comprehend the principle of change.

units.zh: 臣息農收集故營，以備不虞，而石越傾鄴城之眾，輕相掩襲，兵陣未交，越已隕首。
units.en: My son Nong rallied our old camps; Shi Yue struck lightly from Ye and was killed before battle was joined.
units.literal: Your servant's son Nong gathered the old camps to guard against the unforeseen, while Shi Yue led the host of Ye city and lightly made a surprise attack—the battle lines had not yet met when Yue already fell head.

units.zh: 臣既單車懸軫，歸者如雲，斯實天符，非臣之力。
units.en: I came with a single cart and men returned like clouds—this was heaven, not my power.
units.literal: Your servant came alone in a single carriage and those returning were like clouds—this was truly heaven's sign, not your servant's strength.

units.zh: 且鄴者臣國舊都，應即惠及，然後西面受制，永守東籓，上成陛下遇臣之意，下全愚臣感報之誠。
units.en: Ye is my old capital and should be won with kindness; then I will serve you in the east, fulfilling your grace and my debt.
units.literal: Moreover Ye is your servant's former capital and should immediately receive favor; then westward submit to command and forever guard the eastern frontier, above fulfilling Your Majesty's intent toward your servant, below completing your foolish servant's debt of grateful return.

units.zh: 今進師圍鄴，並喻丕以天時人事。
units.en: Now I besiege Ye and teach Pi the times.
units.literal: Now advancing the army to besiege Ye, I also instruct Pi on heaven's season and human affairs.

units.zh: 而丕不察機運，杜門自守，時出挑戰，鋒戈屢交，恆恐飛矢誤中，以傷陛下天性之念。
units.en: Pi will not read the times; he shuts his gates and fights; blades cross daily—I fear a stray arrow may wound the bond you bear him.
units.literal: Yet Pi does not discern the turn of fortune, shuts his gates and holds defense, sometimes coming out to challenge; blades and spears repeatedly cross—I ever fear stray arrows may wound Your Majesty's nature of kin.

units.zh: 臣之此誠，未簡神聽，輒遏兵止銳，不敢竊攻。
units.en: This sincerity has not reached you; I hold my army back and dare not strike in secret.
units.literal: Your servant's this sincerity has not reached divine hearing; I therefore hold the army and blunt its edge, not daring to attack in secret.

units.zh: 夫運有推移，去來常事，惟陛下察之。」
units.en: Fortune turns; what comes and goes is constant—may Your Majesty judge."
units.literal: Fortune has its shifts; coming and going are constant affairs—may Your Majesty examine this."

units.zh: 堅報曰：「朕以不德，忝承靈命，君臨萬邦，三十年矣。
units.en: Fu Jian answered: "With little virtue I have borne the mandate thirty years.
units.literal: Jian replied, "We with little virtue have presumptuously received the bright mandate and for thirty years have faced the myriad realms.

units.zh: 遐方幽裔，莫不來庭，惟東南一隅，敢違王命。
units.en: Far peoples have come to court; only the southeast dared defy me.
units.literal: Distant lands and secluded tribes have all come to court; only the southeast corner dared defy the royal command.

units.zh: 朕爰奮六師，恭行天罰，而玄機不吊，王師敗績。
units.en: I raised the Six Armies to punish them, yet heaven was unkind and my host was broken.
units.literal: We then roused the Six Armies and reverently executed heaven's punishment, yet the mysterious pivot was unkind and the royal army was defeated.

units.zh: 賴卿忠誠之至，輔翼朕躬，社稷之不隕，卿之力也。
units.en: By your loyalty you saved me and the altars did not fall—that was your doing.
units.literal: Relying on your loyalty to the utmost, assisting and supporting Our person, that the altars did not fall was your strength.

units.zh: 《詩》云：『中心藏之，何日忘之。』
units.en: The Odes say, "I hide it in my heart—when shall I forget?"
units.literal: The Odes say, "Hidden in the center—when shall I forget it."

units.zh: 方任卿以元相，爵卿以郡侯，庶弘濟艱難，敬酬勳烈，何圖伯夷忽毀冰操，柳惠倏為淫夫！
units.en: I would have made you chief minister and marquis of a commandery to repay your merit—why has Bo Yi shattered his honor and Liuxia Hui turned debauched!
units.literal: We were about to entrust you with the office of chief minister and enfeoff you as marquis of a commandery, hoping broadly to cross hardship and respectfully repay your merit—why has Bo Yi suddenly destroyed his icy integrity and Liuxia Hui instantly become a debauched man!

units.zh: 覽表惋然，有慚朝士。
units.en: Your letter grieves and shames me before my court.
units.literal: Reading your memorial We are grieved and ashamed before the courtiers.

units.zh: 卿既不容於本朝，匹馬而投命，朕則寵卿以將位，禮卿以上賓，任同舊臣，爵齊勳輔，歃血斷金，披心相付。
units.en: Driven from your own court you came to me; I made you a general and chief guest, equal to my greatest servants, joined in oath and trust.
units.literal: You were not tolerated in your native court, came on a single horse and entrusted your life; We then favored you with a general's post and honored you as a chief guest, entrusted you as an old minister, ranks equal to the greatest helpers, blood-oath and severed metal, heart opened and entrusted.

units.zh: 謂卿食椹懷音，保之偕老。
units.en: I said you would keep faith to the end like the bird that eats mulberry.
units.literal: We said you would eat mulberry and cherish the tune, keep faith to the end.

units.zh: 豈意畜水覆舟，養獸反害，悔之噬臍，將何所及！
units.en: Who thought the water you carried would sink the boat, the beast you fed would bite the hand—regret gnaws to the marrow!
units.literal: Who thought overturned water would cover the boat, nurtured beasts would turn to harm—regret bites to the navel, what is there to reach!

units.zh: 誕言駭眾，誇擬非常，周武之事，豈卿庸人所可論哉！
units.en: Your boasts shock the world and ape King Wu—how dare a man like you speak of such things!
units.literal: Wild words shock the masses, boasting imitates the extraordinary; the affairs of King Wu—how can a mediocre man like you discuss them!

units.zh: 失籠之鳥，非羅所羈；
units.en: A bird out of the cage is not caught by the net;
units.literal: A bird escaped its cage is not held by the net;

units.zh: 脫網之鯨，豈罟所制！
units.en: a whale off the line is not held by the weir!
units.literal: a whale escaped the seine is not checked by the weir!

units.zh: 翹陸任懷，何須聞也。
units.en: Let the beast of the heights go where it will—I need not hear more.
units.literal: Let soaring land beasts follow their bent—why need We hear of it.

units.zh: 念卿垂老，老而為賊，生為叛臣，死為逆鬼，侏張幽顯，布毒存亡，中原士女，何痛如之！
units.en: At seventy you turn bandit, live a traitor, die a rebel, poison the living and dead—the pain of the central plains, what pain like it!
units.literal: Thinking of you in old age, old yet becoming a bandit, alive a rebellious minister, dead a rebellious ghost, spreading poison through hidden and manifest, sowing poison through survival and extinction—the scholars of the central plains, what pain like this!

units.zh: 朕之曆運興喪，豈復由卿！
units.en: Whether my house stands or falls—how is that your doing!
units.literal: Our dynasty's rise and fall—how could it again be because of you!

units.zh: 但長樂、平原以未立之年，遇卿於兩都，慮其經略未稱朕心，所恨者此焉而已。」
units.en: Only for Changle and Pingyuan, still young when they met you in the Two Capitals—we regret their counsel was not to our mind; that is all."
units.literal: Only the Duke of Changle and the Duke of Pingyuan, in years not yet established, met you in the Two Capitals—we regret that their planning and conduct did not match Our heart; this is the only thing regretted."

units.zh: 垂攻拔鄴郛，丕固守中城，垂塹而圍之，分遣老弱于魏郡、肥鄉，築新興城以置輜重，擁漳水以灌之。
units.en: Chui took Ye's outer wall; Pi held the inner city; Chui moated and besieged, moved the weak to Weijun and Feixiang, built Xinxing for stores, and dammed the Zhang to flood the city.
units.literal: Chui took the outer wall of Ye; Pi firmly held the inner city; Chui moated and besieged it, sent the old and weak to Weijun and Feixiang, built Xinxing city to place baggage, and dammed the Zhang River to flood it.

units.zh: 翟斌潛諷丁零及西人，請斌為尚書令。
units.en: Zhai Bin secretly urged the Dingling and western troops to make him Director of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: Zhai Bin secretly incited the Dingling and western men to ask that Bin be made Director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 垂訪之群僚，其安東將軍封衡厲色曰：「馬能千里，不免羈靽，明畜生不可以人禦也。
units.en: Chui asked his officers; Feng Heng said sharply, "A horse may run a thousand li but needs the bridle—a bright beast is not driven like a man.
units.literal: Chui consulted the officials; his General Who Pacifies the East Feng Heng said sternly, "A horse can run a thousand li but cannot escape bridle and rein—a bright beast cannot be driven like a man.

units.zh: 斌戎狄小人，遭時際會，兄弟封王，自驩兜已來，未有此福。
units.en: Bin is a barbarian who met his hour; brothers made kings—since Huandou there has been no such fortune.
units.literal: Bin is a barbarian of the Rong and Di, meeting the fortune of the times; brothers enfeoffed as kings—since Huandou there has been no such blessing.

units.zh: 忽履盈忘止，復有斯求，魂爽錯亂，必死不出年也。」
units.en: Drunk on fortune he forgets his limit and asks for more—his mind is lost and he will not live out the year."
units.literal: Suddenly treading fullness he forgets stop, again making this request—his soul is disordered and he will surely die within the year."

units.zh: 垂猶隱忍容之，令曰：「翟王之功宜居上輔，但台既未建，此官不可便置。
units.en: Chui still bore with him and said, "Prince Zhai's merit deserves the highest post, but the Secretariat is not yet built and the office cannot be given now.
units.literal: Chui still concealed and tolerated him, issuing an order, "Prince Zhai's merit should occupy the highest assistant post, but the terrace is not yet built and this office cannot be set at once.

units.zh: 待六合廓清，更當議之。」
units.en: When the realm is pacified we will speak of it again."
units.literal: When the six realms are cleared, we shall discuss it again."

units.zh: 斌怒，密應苻丕，潛使丁零決防潰水。
units.en: Bin in anger secretly aided Fu Pi and had the Dingling breach the dike.
units.literal: Bin was angry and secretly responded to Fu Pi; secretly he had the Dingling break the dike and release the flood.

units.zh: 事泄，垂誅之。
units.en: The plot was discovered and Chui killed him.
units.literal: The affair leaked; Chui executed him.

units.zh: 斌兄子真率其部眾北走邯鄲，引兵向鄴，欲與丕為內外之勢，垂令其太子寶、冠軍慕容隆擊破之。
units.en: Bin's nephew Zhen fled north to Handan and marched on Ye, intending to coordinate with Pi from outside and inside; Chui sent Bao and Murong Long to break him.
units.literal: Bin's nephew Zhen led his tribal host north to Handan and led troops toward Ye intending inside-out cooperation with Pi; Chui ordered his Heir Bao and the Champion Murong Long to defeat them.

units.zh: 真自邯鄲北走，又使慕容楷率騎追之，戰於下邑，為真所敗，真遂屯于承營。
units.en: Zhen fled north from Handan, so Chui sent Murong Kai in pursuit with cavalry. They fought at Xiayi; Zhen defeated him and then camped at Chengying.
units.literal: Zhen fled north from Handan; Chui again sent Murong Kai with cavalry to pursue him. They fought at Xiayi, Kai was defeated by Zhen, and Zhen then camped at Chengying.

units.zh: 垂謂諸將曰：「苻丕窮寇，必守死不降。
units.en: Chui told his officers, "Fu Pi is cornered and will die before he yields.
units.literal: Chui told the generals, "Fu Pi is a cornered bandit and will surely hold death and not surrender.

units.zh: 丁零叛擾，乃我腹心之患。
units.en: The rebellious Dingling are the trouble at our heart.
units.literal: The Dingling in rebellion and disorder are the trouble of our heart and belly.

units.zh: 吾欲遷師新城，開其逸路，進以謝秦主疇昔之恩，退以嚴擊真之備。」
units.en: I will move to Xincheng, open their escape, advance to repay Qin's old grace, retreat to crush Zhen."
units.literal: I wish to shift the army to Xincheng, open their escape route, advance to repay the Qin sovereign's former grace, retreat to strike hard against Zhen's preparations."

units.zh: 於是引師去鄴，北屯新城。
units.en: He withdrew from Ye and camped at Xincheng.
units.literal: Thereupon he led the army from Ye and encamped north at Xincheng.

units.zh: 慕容農進攻翟嵩于黃泥，破之。
units.en: Murong Nong defeated Zhai Song at Huangni.
units.literal: Murong Nong attacked Zhai Song at Huangni and defeated him.

units.zh: 垂謂其范陽王德曰：「苻丕吾縱之不能去，方引晉師規固鄴都，不可置也。」
units.en: Chui told Murong De, "I spared Fu Pi and he would not go; now he calls Jin to hold Ye—he cannot remain."
units.literal: Chui told his Prince of Fanyang De, "Fu Pi I let go and he would not leave; now he draws Jin troops to hold Ye—he cannot be left."

units.zh: 進師又攻鄴，開其西奔之路。
units.en: He marched on Ye again and opened the western road for flight.
units.literal: Advancing the army he again attacked Ye and opened the western route of flight.

units.zh: 垂將有北都中山之意，農率眾數萬迎之。
units.en: Chui planned to set his northern capital at Zhongshan; Nong came out with tens of thousands to meet him.
units.literal: Chui intended to make Zhongshan the northern capital; Nong led tens of thousands to welcome him.

units.zh: 群僚聞慕容暐為苻堅所殺，勸垂僭位。
units.en: When they heard Murong Wei had been killed by Fu Jian, his officers urged him to take the throne.
units.literal: The officials, hearing Murong Wei had been killed by Fu Jian, urged Chui to usurp the throne.

units.zh: 垂以慕容沖稱號關中，不許。
units.en: Murong Chong had already declared himself in Guanzhong, and Chui would not follow suit.
units.literal: Chui, because Murong Chong had styled himself in Guanzhong, did not permit it.

units.zh: 晉龍驤將軍劉牢之率眾救苻丕，至鄴，垂逆戰，敗績，遂撤鄴圍，退屯新城。
units.en: Liu Laozhi of Jin marched to relieve Fu Pi; Chui fought him at Ye, lost, lifted the siege, and withdrew to Xincheng.
units.literal: The Jin Dragon-soaring General Liu Laozhi led his host to rescue Fu Pi; reaching Ye, Chui met him in battle, was defeated, and thereupon raised the siege of Ye and withdrew to encamp at Xincheng.

units.zh: 垂自新城北走，牢之追垂，連戰皆敗。
units.en: Chui fled north; Laozhi pursued but was defeated again and again.
units.literal: Chui fled north from Xincheng; Laozhi pursued him but was defeated in every successive battle.

units.zh: 又戰於五橋澤，王師敗績，德及隆引兵要之於五丈橋，牢之馳馬跳五丈澗，會苻丕救至而免。
units.en: At Wuqiao Marsh the Jin army broke; De and Long blocked Wuzhang Bridge; Laozhi leaped the ravine and escaped when Fu Pi came up.
units.literal: Again they fought at Wuqiao Marsh; the royal army was defeated; De and Long led troops to intercept at Wuzhang Bridge; Laozhi spurred his horse and leaped the Wuzhang ravine, and was spared when Fu Pi's rescue arrived.

units.zh: 翟真去承營，徙屯行唐，真司馬鮮于乞殺真，盡誅翟氏，自立為趙王。
units.en: Zhai Zhen moved to Xingtang; his officer Xianyu Qi killed him, wiped out the Zhai line, and made himself king of Zhao.
units.literal: Zhai Zhen left Chengying and moved camp to Xingtang; Zhen's Major Xianyu Qi killed Zhen, exterminated the Zhai clan, and set himself up as King of Zhao.

units.zh: 營人攻殺乞，迎立真從弟成為主，真子遼奔黎陽。
units.en: The camp killed Qi and set up Cheng; Zhen's son Liao fled to Liyang.
units.literal: The camp soldiers attacked and killed Qi, welcomed Zhen's cousin Cheng as chief, and Zhen's son Liao fled to Liyang.

units.zh: 高句驪寇遼東，垂平北慕容佐遣司馬郝景率眾救之，為高句驪所敗，遼東、玄菟遂沒。
units.en: Koguryo invaded Liaodong; Murong Zuo sent Hao Jing to relieve it and was beaten; Liaodong and Xuantu fell.
units.literal: Koguryo raided Liaodong; Chui's Pacifier of the North Murong Zuo sent the Major Hao Jing to lead troops to rescue; they were defeated by Koguryo, and Liaodong and Xuantu were lost.

units.zh: 建節將軍徐岩叛于武邑，驅掠四千餘人，北走幽州。
units.en: Xu Yan rebelled at Wuyi, seized four thousand people, and fled north to Youzhou.
units.literal: The General Who Establishes the Standard Xu Yan rebelled at Wuyi, drove off and plundered more than four thousand people, and fled north to Youzhou.

units.zh: 垂馳敕其將平規曰：「但固守勿戰，比破丁零，吾當自討之。」
units.en: Chui ordered Ping Gui, "Hold fast and do not give battle; when I have finished the Dingling I will come myself."
units.literal: Chui urgently ordered his general Ping Gui, "Only hold and do not fight; when I have broken the Dingling I myself will attack."

units.zh: 規違命距戰，為岩所敗。
units.en: Gui disobeyed, gave battle, and was routed.
units.literal: Gui disobeyed the order and faced battle and was defeated by Yan.

units.zh: 岩乘勝入薊，掠千餘戶而去，所過寇暴，遂據令支。
units.en: Yan stormed Ji, looted a thousand households, and seized Lingzhi.
units.literal: Yan took advantage of victory to enter Ji, plundered more than a thousand households and left; wherever he passed he raided violently, and then held Lingzhi.

units.zh: 翟成長史鮮于得斬成而降，垂入行唐，悉坑其眾。
units.en: Xianyu De killed Cheng and surrendered; Chui entered Xingtang and massacred his army.
units.literal: Zhai Cheng's Chief Clerk Xianyu De beheaded Cheng and surrendered; Chui entered Xingtang and buried alive all his host.

units.zh: 苻丕棄鄴城，奔於并州。
units.en: Fu Pi abandoned Ye and fled to Bingzhou.
units.literal: Fu Pi abandoned Ye city and fled to Bingzhou.

units.zh: 慕容農攻克令支，斬徐岩兄弟。
units.en: Murong Nong took Lingzhi and executed Xu Yan and his brothers.
units.literal: Murong Nong took Lingzhi and beheaded Xu Yan and his brothers.

units.zh: 時伐高句驪，復遼東、玄菟二郡，還屯龍城。
units.en: He campaigned against Koguryo, recovered Liaodong and Xuantu, and returned to Longcheng.
units.literal: At that time campaigning against Koguryo, he recovered Liaodong and Xuantu, returned to camp at Longcheng.

units.zh: 垂定都中山，群僚勸即尊號，具典儀，修郊燎之禮。
units.en: Chui made Zhongshan his capital. His officials urged him to take the throne, prepared the full ceremonial protocol, and arranged the suburban sacrificial rites.
units.literal: Chui established the capital at Zhongshan; the assembled officials urged him to assume the imperial title, prepared the ceremonial regulations, and arranged the suburban sacrifice rites.

units.zh: 垂從之，乙太元十一年僭即位。
units.en: Chui agreed; in the eleventh year of the Taiyuan era he unlawfully took the throne.
units.literal: Chui followed this; in the eleventh year of the Taiyuan era he usurped enthronement.

units.zh: 赦其境內，改元曰建興，置百官，繕宗廟社稷，立寶為太子。
units.en: He granted an amnesty throughout his realm, adopted the era name Jianxing, established the full bureaucracy, restored the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain, and named Bao crown prince.
units.literal: He proclaimed amnesty within his borders, changed the era name to Jianxing, established the hundred officials, repaired the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain, and installed Bao as crown prince.

units.zh: 以其左長史庫辱官偉、右長史段崇、龍驤張崇，中山尹封衡為吏部尚書，慕容德為侍中、都督中外諸軍事、領司隸校尉，撫軍慕容麟為衛大將軍，其餘拜授有差。
units.en: He appointed Kuruguan Wei Left Chief Clerk, Duan Chong Right Chief Clerk, and Zhang Chong Dragon-Prancing General; he made Feng Heng, Governor of Zhongshan, Minister of Personnel; Murong De Palace Attendant, Commander of All Armies Inside and Outside, and concurrently Colonel-Director of Retainers; and the Pacifying General Murong Lin Grand General of the Guards. The rest received posts by rank.
units.literal: He appointed Kuruguan Wei Left Chief Clerk, Duan Chong Right Chief Clerk, and Zhang Chong Dragon-Prancing General; he made Feng Heng, Administrator of Zhongshan, Minister of Personnel; Murong De Palace Attendant, Commander of All Armies Within and Without, and concurrently Colonel-Director of Retainers; and the Pacifying General Murong Lin Grand General of the Guards. The rest received appointments according to rank.

units.zh: 追尊母蘭氏為文昭皇后，遷皝後段氏，以蘭氏配饗。
units.en: He posthumously honored his mother Lady Lan as Empress Wenzhao, displaced Empress Duan, Huang's former consort, and paired Lady Lan for ancestral sacrifice alongside Huang.
units.literal: He posthumously honored his mother Lady Lan as Empress Wenzhao, removed Empress Duan, consort of Huang, and paired Lady Lan for joint sacrifice.

units.zh: 博士劉詳、董謐議以堯母妃位第三，不以貴陵薑嫄，明聖王之道以至公為先。
units.en: The erudites Liu Xiang and Dong Mi argued that Yao's mother ranked only third among the consorts and did not use her honored status to outrank Jiang Yuan, showing that the way of sage-kings put perfect impartiality first.
units.literal: The Erudites Liu Xiang and Dong Mi argued that Yao's mother occupied the third rank among the consorts and did not use her honored status to outrank Jiang Yuan, showing that the way of sage-kings puts perfect impartiality first.

units.zh: 垂不從。
units.en: Chui rejected their counsel.
units.literal: Chui did not follow this.

units.zh: 遣其征西慕容楷、衛軍慕容麟、鎮南慕容紹、征虜慕容宙等攻苻堅冀州牧苻定、鎮東苻紹、幽州牧苻謨、鎮北苻亮。
units.en: He sent Kai, Lin, Shao, and Zhou against Fu Jian's governors Fu Ding, Fu Shao, Fu Mo, and Fu Liang.
units.literal: He sent his General Who Conquers the West Murong Kai, the Guards Murong Lin, the Pacifier of the South Murong Shao, and the General Who Punishes the Barbarians Murong Zhou and others to attack Fu Jian's Governor of Jizhou Fu Ding, the Pacifier of the East Fu Shao, the Governor of Youzhou Fu Mo, and the Pacifier of the North Fu Liang.

units.zh: 楷與定等書，喻以禍福，定等悉降。
units.en: Kai wrote to them of fortune and ruin, and all surrendered.
units.literal: Kai wrote to Ding and the others, instructing them in fortune and calamity, and Ding and the others all surrendered.

units.zh: 垂留其太子寶守中山，率諸將南攻翟遼，以楷為前鋒都督。
units.en: Leaving Bao at Zhongshan, Chui marched south against Zhai Liao with Kai in the van.
units.literal: Chui left his Heir Bao to guard Zhongshan and led the generals south to attack Zhai Liao, with Kai as commander of the vanguard.

units.zh: 遼之部眾皆燕、趙人也，咸曰：「太原王之子，吾之父母。」
units.en: Liao's men were Yan and Zhao folk; they said, "The Prince of Taiyuan's son is our father and mother."
units.literal: Liao's tribal host were all men of Yan and Zhao; they all said, "The son of the Prince of Taiyuan is our father and mother."

units.zh: 相率歸附。
units.en: They came over in crowds.
units.literal: They joined one another in returning to allegiance.

units.zh: 遼懼，遣使請降。
units.en: Liao in terror sent an envoy to request surrender.
units.literal: Liao in fear sent envoys to ask surrender.

units.zh: 垂至黎陽，遼肉袒謝罪，垂厚撫之。
units.en: At Liyang, Liao came bare-chested to submit, and Chui treated him kindly.
units.literal: Chui reached Liyang; Liao bared his torso in confession of guilt, and Chui treated him generously.

units.zh: 為其太子寶起承華觀，以寶錄尚書政事，巨細皆委之，重總大綱而已。
units.en: He built the Chenghua Tower for Bao, gave him charge of the secretariat, and kept only the larger design in his own hands.
units.literal: For his Heir Bao he built the Chenghua Tower; Bao recorded the Master of Writing's affairs, and great and small were all entrusted to him—Chui himself held only the great outline.

units.zh: 立其夫人段氏為皇后。
units.en: He made his consort Lady Duan empress.
units.literal: He installed his consort Lady Duan as empress.

units.zh: 又以寶領侍中、大單于、驃騎大將軍、幽州牧。
units.en: He made Bao Palace Attendant, Grand Chanyu, General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Youzhou.
units.literal: He also made Bao Palace Attendant, Grand Chanyu, General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Youzhou.

units.zh: 建留台于龍城，以高陽王慕容隆錄留台尚書事。
units.en: He set up the Rear Secretariat at Longcheng under Murong Long.
units.literal: He established the Rear Secretariat at Longcheng, with the Prince of Gaoyang Murong Long recording the affairs of the Rear Secretariat.

units.zh: 時慕容暐及諸宗室為苻堅所害者，並招魂葬之。
units.en: He buried by ceremony those of the Murong clan whom Fu Jian had killed.
units.literal: At that time Murong Wei and the clansmen killed by Fu Jian were all summoned in spirit and buried.

units.zh: 清河太守賀耕聚眾定陵以叛，南應翟遼，慕容農討斬之，毀定陵城。
units.en: He Geng of Qinghe rebelled at Dingling and joined Zhai Liao; Murong Nong destroyed him and razed Dingling.
units.literal: The Administrator of Qinghe He Geng gathered a host at Dingling and rebelled, responding to Zhai Liao in the south; Murong Nong attacked and beheaded him and destroyed Dingling city.

units.zh: 進師入鄴，以鄴城廣難固，築鳳陽門大道之東為隔城。
units.en: He entered Ye, and because the city was too wide to defend easily, built a new quarter east of the Fengyang Gate.
units.literal: Advancing the army into Ye, because Ye city was broad and hard to fortify, he built a separate city east of the Fengyang Gate avenue.

units.zh: 其尚書郎婁會上疏曰：「三年之喪，天下之達制，兵荒殺禮，遂以一切取士。
units.en: Lou Hui of the Masters of Writing wrote, "Three years' mourning is the law of the realm; war has killed ritual, and men seize office without waiting.
units.literal: His Master of Writing Gentleman Lou Hui memorialized, "The three-year mourning is the universal rule of the realm; war and disorder have killed ritual, and so everything has been taken at once for scholars.

units.zh: 人心奔兢，苟求榮進，至乃身冒縗絰，以赴時役，豈必殉忠於國家，亦昧利於其間也。
units.en: Men rush for rank, even wearing mourning to take post—whether from loyalty or from greed who can tell?
units.literal: Men's hearts race in competition, hastening to seek honor and advancement—even wearing hemp and rushing to seasonal corvée; are they surely loyal to the state, or do they also covet profit in the midst?

units.zh: 聖王設教，不以顛沛而虧其道，不以喪亂而變其化，故能杜豪兢之門，塞奔波之路。
units.en: A sage king does not let hardship void his teaching nor disorder change his rule; he closes the door to reckless ambition and the road of flight.
units.literal: The sage king establishes teaching and does not let the teaching be impaired by hardship, does not change his transformation because of disorder—therefore he can shut the gate of fierce competition and block the road of flight.

units.zh: 陛下鐘百王之季，廓中興之業，天下漸平，兵革方偃，誠宜蠲蕩瑕穢，率由舊章。
units.en: Your Majesty has raised a restored age; the realm grows quiet and arms are stilled—you should cleanse these abuses and return to the old statutes.
units.literal: Your Majesty at the end of the hundred kings has expanded the work of restoration; the realm is gradually pacified and arms are about to be laid down—truly you should sweep away blemishes and follow the old statutes.

units.zh: 吏遭大喪，聽終三年之禮，則四方知化，人斯服禮。」
units.en: Let officials observe full mourning for parents, and the realm will learn ritual again."
units.literal: When officials meet great mourning, let them be permitted the full three-year rite, then the four quarters will know transformation and men will submit to ritual."

units.zh: 垂不從。
units.en: Chui refused.
units.literal: Chui did not follow this.

units.zh: 翟遼死，子釗代立，攻逼鄴城，慕容農擊走之。
units.en: When Zhai Liao died, his son Zhao attacked Ye and was driven off by Murong Nong.
units.literal: Zhai Liao died; his son Zhao succeeded and attacked Ye; Murong Nong drove him off.

units.zh: 垂引師伐釗於滑台，次於黎陽津，釗于南岸距守，諸將惡其兵精，咸諫不宜濟河。
units.en: Chui marched on Zhao at Huatai and camped at Liyang ford; Zhao held the south bank; his officers feared Zhao's sharp troops and urged him not to cross.
units.literal: Chui led troops to attack Zhao at Huatai, halted at the Liyang ford; Zhao held the south bank in defense; the generals hated his troops' keen edge and all remonstrated that crossing the river was inadvisable.

units.zh: 垂笑曰：「堅子何能為，吾今為鯽等殺之。」
units.en: Chui smiled and said, "What can this brat do? I shall kill him for you all."
units.literal: Chui smiled and said, "How can this brat accomplish anything—I shall kill him for you all."

units.zh: 遂徙營就西津，為牛皮船百餘艘，載疑兵列杖，溯流而上。
units.en: He moved to the western crossing, built a hundred oxhide boats loaded with dummy spearmen, and sent them upstream.
units.literal: Thereupon he shifted camp to the western ford, made more than a hundred oxhide boats, loaded decoy troops with poles, and went upstream.

units.zh: 釗先以大眾備黎陽，見垂向西津，乃棄營西距。
units.en: Zhao had massed at Liyang; seeing Chui move west, he marched west to block him.
units.literal: Zhao first with a great host prepared at Liyang; seeing Chui go to the western ford, he abandoned camp and went west to block.

units.zh: 垂潛遣其桂林王慕容鎮、驃騎慕容國于黎陽津夜濟，壁于河南。
units.en: Chui secretly sent Murong Zhen and Murong Guo to cross by night and fortify south of the river.
units.literal: Chui secretly sent his Prince of Guilin Murong Zhen and the Agile Cavalry Murong Guo to cross at the Liyang ford by night and wall on the south of the river.

units.zh: 釗聞而奔還，士眾疲渴，走歸滑台，釗攜妻子率數百騎北趣白鹿山。
units.en: Zhao turned back; his men, spent and thirsty, fled to Huatai; Zhao took his family and a few hundred horse and ran for Bailu Mountain.
units.literal: Zhao heard and ran back; the soldiers were weary and thirsty, fled back to Huatai; Zhao took wife and children and led several hundred horsemen north toward Bailu Mountain.

units.zh: 農追擊，盡擒其眾，釗單騎奔長子。
units.en: Nong pursued and took them all; Zhao alone escaped to Changzi.
units.literal: Nong pursued, captured all his host; Zhao alone on a single horse fled to Changzi.

units.zh: 釗所統七郡戶三萬八千皆安堵如故。
units.en: The seven commanderies, thirty-eight thousand households, were left undisturbed.
units.literal: The seven commanderies under Zhao's rule, thirty-eight thousand households, were all settled as before.

units.zh: 徙徐州流人七千餘戶于黎陽。
units.en: He resettled seven thousand refugees from Xuzhou at Liyang.
units.literal: He moved seven thousand more households of refugees from Xuzhou to Liyang.

units.zh: 於是議征長子。
units.en: Then they debated an attack on Changzi.
units.literal: Thereupon they deliberated attacking Changzi.

units.zh: 諸將咸諫，以慕容永未有釁，連歲征役，士卒疲怠，請俟他年。
units.en: His officers objected that Murong Yong had given no cause, that years of war had exhausted the troops, and begged to wait.
units.literal: The generals all remonstrated that Murong Yong had not yet given offense, and year after year campaigns had wearied the soldiers— they asked to wait for another year.

units.zh: 垂將從之，及聞慕容德之策，笑曰：「吾計決矣。
units.en: He was about to agree; then he heard Murong De's counsel and said, "My mind is made up.
units.literal: Chui was about to follow this; when he heard Murong De's plan he smiled and said, "My decision is made.

units.zh: 且吾投老，扣囊底智，足以克之，不復留逆賊以累子孫也。」
units.en: I am old, but what wisdom remains in the bottom of the bag is enough to crush him—I will not leave this rebel to my heirs."
units.literal: Moreover I am old; tapping the bottom of the bag's wisdom is enough to overcome him—I will not leave this rebel to burden my sons and grandsons."

units.zh: 乃發步騎七萬，遣其丹陽王慕容贊、龍驤張崇攻永弟支于晉陽。
units.en: He sent seventy thousand men, and Murong Zan and Zhang Chong against Yong's brother Zhi at Jinyang.
units.literal: Thereupon he sent seventy thousand foot and horse, dispatched his Prince of Danyang Murong Zan and the Dragon-soaring Zhang Chong to attack Yong's younger brother Zhi at Jinyang.

units.zh: 永遣其將刁雲、慕容鐘率眾五萬屯潞川。
units.en: Yong sent Diao Yun and Murong Zhong with fifty thousand to hold Luchuan.
units.literal: Yong sent his generals Diao Yun and Murong Zhong with fifty thousand to encamp at Luchuan.

units.zh: 垂遣慕容楷出自滏口，慕容農入自壺關，垂頓於鄴之西南，月餘不進。
units.en: Chui sent Kai through Fukou and Nong through Huguan, and himself camped southwest of Ye for a month without moving.
